newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber futures end down in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber futures end down in slow trade.

text.p: Rubber futures closed lower on Monday in slow, thin trade with players discouraged by the absence of major offtake in the market, dealers said.
"There was some buying by local dealers for RSS3 rubber, but there was little else in the other rubber brands," a trader for a Singapore-based commodity house said.
"Some people were hoping for a lift from the spot expiry in Japan today, but nothing happened. Instead, prices in Japan fell," another dealer said.
Tokyo's benchmark July contract shed 3.1 yen to settle at 151.0 while Kobe's July contract dipped 0.1 yen to end at 151.1.
Total volume traded for RSS3 rubber reached about 2,000 tonnes against less than 300 tonnes each for RSS1 and TSR20 rubber, traders said.
At around 0945 GMT, April RSS3 was seen at 120.00-122.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 122.00 cents.
April RSS1 was indicated at 170.00-172.00 Singapore cents (US$1.20-$1.21) a kg from last Friday's settlement of 172.25 cents.
April TSR20 was seen at 168.00 Singapore cents (US$1.18) a kg from the previous 168.50 cents.
